text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Brighton and Hove Albion and West Ham at the Amex Stadium.

After qualifying for European football for the first time ever by finishing sixth last season, the Seagulls have started this campaign in similarly impressive fashion with a pair of 4-1 victories, at home to newly promoted Luton Town and then away at Wolves.
Back on home soil, they will be looking to make it three wins from three and move themselves top of the Premier League in the process, until Sunday at least.

The Hammers will also look back fondly on last term after winning the Europa Conference League, though that masked a poor Premier League campaign in which they recorded a 14th-placed finish, their lowest since the 2019-20 season.
However, a positive start has seen them draw at Bournemouth and claim a stunning 3-1 victory over Chelsea, and Irons fans will be hoping to continue their unbeaten start here.

Roberto De Zerbi makes two changes from the win at Molineux as Verbruggen comes in for his Premier League debut between the sticks with Steele dropping to the bench, while Ferguson replaces the injured Julio Enciso.
David Moyes also goes with a pair of alterations from his team's last outing as Ogbonna starts in place of Nayef Aguerd, who was sent off against Chelsea after receiving two yellow cards.
Alvarez also makes his full debut in place of Benrahma.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch ahead of what should be another exciting Premier League encounter!
Brighton kick us off and we are underway at the Amex Stadium!
An early chance for the visitors goes begging as a long throw ends up bouncing to the back post for Paqueta, who blazes over from close range.
It has been a lively start as both teams look to get on the front foot, which bodes well for the neutral.
CHANCE! Paqueta shows his class by playing a perfectly weighted throughball for Antonio, who decides to send a first-time effort towards goal.
However, the forward's strike does not have the power to trouble Verbruggen, who makes a comfortable save.
The visitors have now had two decent chances despite not having much of the ball in the opening period of this game.
De Zerbi's men will have to tighten up at the back.
A marauding run from Antonio takes him all the way into the Brighton box, but he is eventually slowed down before Estupinan forces him out of play.
The Hammers striker is looking lively, though.

The Seagulls have lost none of their 12 Premier League meetings with West Ham (six wins, six draws) – it is both the most they have faced a side without ever losing and the most the Hammers have faced a side without ever winning in the competition.
Paqueta theatrically goes down clutching his face after being caught with a stray arm by Milner, though he is up and okay to continue.
CLOSE! A sweeping Brighton move sees a diagonal ball brought down excellently by Estupinan before the full-back tees up Gilmour to strike towards goal.
The effort is powerful and has Areola scrambling, though the ball flies the wrong side of the post for the hosts.
Brighton have had 88 per cent of the possession so far in this match, though this stubborn West Ham defence is so far holding firm.
GOAL!!! WEST HAM ARE IN FRONT!!! Antonio again causes problems in the Brighton defence, showing his strength to dispossess Webster before squaring for Ward-Prowse.
The former Southampton man sees his first attempt blocked by Gilmour, but he is alert to latch onto the rebound and smash home.
1-0 to the Hammers!
The Seagulls are nearly level almost immediately as neat footwork from Ferguson opens up the space to shoot, but Areola is able to get down to his right and make a decent stop.
Despite having very little of the ball to this point, West Ham are in front and have a lead to defend.
There is a long way to go though if they are to secure a big three points on the road.
Ward-Prowse receives the first yellow card of the contest for a poor sliding challenge on Gilmour in midfield.
Ward-Prowse has scored four Premier League goals against Brighton and has only netted more against Tottenham (five).
It has been a good response to going behind by De Zerbi's men, though they are still yet to create a real clear-cut chance.
Having put West Ham ahead, Ward-Prowse helps his team at the other end by making a brave block to get in the way of Gilmour's fierce first-time drive.
It is one-way traffic at the moment, with wave after wave of Brighton attacks streaming towards Areola's goal.
This could be a tricky period of the game for the Hammers as De Zerbi's side probe for an equaliser.
There is a nasty collision in the Brighton penalty area as Verbruggen punches a free-kick delivery away from danger, clattering into Soucek in the process.
The game is immediately stopped with both sets of players quick to call for medical attention.
Soucek remains down, and it appears Moyes will be forced into a change here with the Czech Republic international midfielder looking dazed.
Soucek is finally back to his feet and walks off the pitch as play resumes, with West Ham temporarily down to 10 men.
The Hammers change does finally happen as Benrahma comes on for Soucek, who walks straight down the tunnel.
Gross stings the palms of Areola with a fierce drive as West Ham continue to frustrate Brighton and restrict them to long-range attempts.
There's a moment of real panic as Areola inexplicably fails to gather a high ball.
It subsequently bounces in the visitors' box, but much to their relief, the goalkeeper is able to collect at the second attempt before any lurking Brighton attacker can tap home.
There will be four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Alvarez goes in the book for a nasty challenge on Welbeck.
Perhaps more concerning for the Hammers, though, is the fact the Seagulls will have a free-kick in a great shooting position.
The free-kick is wasted as March tries to curl goalwards, only to be blocked behind for a corner off the head of Alvarez in the wall.
HALF-TIME: BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION 0-1 WEST HAM
The half-time whistle blows as West Ham head into the break with a 1-0 lead at the Amex Stadium after Ward-Prowse put them ahead.
They have been under pressure for much of the half but have also looked a threat on the break, with Antonio causing issues in the Brighton defence.
It was his determination that helped them to get their noses in front after 19 minutes, harrying Webster and nicking the ball off him before squaring to Ward-Prowse.

The former Southampton man saw his first attempt blocked but made no mistake with his second, stroking home to give the Hammers a one-goal advantage, a lead they maintain at the break thanks to a dogged defensive display to this point.
Perhaps most concerning for De Zerbi at the interval is that his team have had 83.9 per cent of the ball so far, and yet they have registered just two shots on target.
Moyes' side look happy to sit back and dare Brighton to break them down, something the Seagulls failed to do in the opening 45 minutes.
The Irons get us back underway for the second period.
WHAT A SAVE! Brighton go mighty close to levelling moments after the interval as Mitoma, unusually quiet in the first half, lofts a great cross into the box to pick out Ferguson.
The young striker nods at goal, and it looks to be sneaking into the bottom corner until the diving Areola tips it wide at full stretch.
Welbeck sees a shot from range blocked behind for a corner as the Seagulls continue to fly out of the blocks since the break.
Can they find an equaliser?
A deep corner finds itself at the feet of Mitoma at the back post, but the winger's effort is lashed high over the crossbar.
The home fans scream for a penalty as Estupinan is bundled over by a clumsy Paqueta challenge.
The protests fall on deaf ears, though.
Bowen misses a decent chance as he strides into the box.
The ball bobs up at the crucial time though and means he loses control of his effort, which flies wide of the target.
West Ham are unbeaten in their last five Premier League matches when leading at half-time, winning all of those games.
OVER! Brighton are caught out by a quick free-kick, and Emerson is fed by a clever Benrahma pass.
The left-back fizzes towards goal, and his effort takes a nick off the crossbar before flying out for a goal-kick.
GOAL!!! WEST HAM ARE 2-0 UP!!! It is a quite brilliant goal as a sweeping counter sees Antonio set Benrahma away down the left.
He is short of options at first, but when they finally arrive, Benrahma arrows a delightful ball for Bowen in the box.
The Europa Conference League final hero brings it down superbly, before coolly poking past Verbuggen to put the Hammers well in control.
Benrahma showed patience and quality by picking out Bowen with a superb pass, before his team-mate did the rest.
Chasing the game, De Zerbi looks to his bench.
His first substitution is to bring on Pedro for Welbeck.
Lallana is also on for Gilmour.
After scoring 10 successive goals at the London Stadium, each of Bowen's last two Premier League strikes have been away from home, also netting on the opening matchday away to Bournemouth.

GOAL!!! IT IS 3-0!!! The Hammers are surely on their way to victory now as Antonio puts them three goals to the good! It is sublime again from Bowen, who brings down a long punt upfield by Areola before finding Antonio with a searching pass.
The striker jinks one way and then the other to wrongfoot Webster, before thumping into the bottom corner!
Having doubled his team's lead moments ago, Bowen then plays a huge role in the third goal to pick out Antonio.
Gross forces a decent save out of Areola to tip his left-footed strike behind for a corner.
It is a long way back for Brighton now, but they will give it a go.
Another Brighton penalty shout comes and goes as Mitoma goes down in the box under a Ward-Prowse challenge.
Antonio has now scored in successive Premier League games for the first time since a run of three games in August 2021.
West Ham nearly have a fourth as Antonio latches onto Paqueta's deft throughball, only to lash high over the crossbar.
Milner makes way for Veltman.
March is replaced by Adingra.
This is the fifth time Bowen has scored and assisted in a Premier League game, but only the second time he has done so away from home, previously doing so against Leicester City in February 2022.
The Hammers look on course to record consecutive Premier League victories for the first time since October, when they beat Wolves and Fulham.
Brighton continue to try and find a way back into the game, but this West Ham defence has looked solid and the Seagulls appear to be running out of ideas.
Areola makes a comfortable save to his right to deny Gross' shot from outside the box.
Moyes brings on centre-back Kehrer for Antonio in a defensive change as West Ham look to see the game out.
CROSSBAR! West Ham are inches away from a fourth as another quick counter sees Benrahma and Ward-Prowse combine.
The latter then smashes a cross in, and Verbruggen is forced to beat away.
However, it deflects off Dunk, and comes off the top of the woodwork.
GOAL!!! Brighton have a goal back! Gross receives the ball outside the penalty area and cuts onto his right foot.
He drills towards goal, and it flies past the diving Areola into the bottom corner to close the deficit to two goals with the scoreline 3-1 to the visitors.
Will it be a consolation or the start of an incredible comeback?
Veltman fed the ball to Gross, who lashed home to give Brighton hope.
The home fans want a penalty as the ball comes off Coufal's hand in the right-back's attempt to block a cross, but again the referee waves play on.
Alvarez's full Premier League debut is over as he is replaced by Fornals.
Ings also comes on for Paqueta.
Gross has now scored 27 Premier League goals for Brighton, more than any other player in the club's history.
WHAT A STOP! Areola makes a vital save to deny Veltman's fierce volley as Brighton threaten to further close the deficit.
That could have really set up a grandstand finish.
Mitoma is booked for a cynical challenge on Bowen.
Kehrer receives a yellow card for bundling over Mitoma.
The fourth official puts up his board and indicates there will be six minutes of additional time at the end of this contest.
Can the Hammers see it out for a huge three points on their travels?
AREOLA AGAIN! The West Ham goalkeeper makes another sublime stop.
Ferguson receives the ball in the box before unleashing a fierce drive at goal.
Somehow though, Areola manages to tip the ball over the crossbar to preserve his team's two-goal advantage.
CLOSE! A corner is nodded powerfully at goal by Dunk, and it looks to be flying in until Ings heads it over his crossbar.
The ball comes out to Dunk and the crowd implores him to shoot from range.
He does exactly that, but it proves to be a poor decision as his effort is blazed high over the crossbar.
The visitors are keeping the ball well as the seconds continue to tick down.
They are moments from victory.
Bowen could and maybe should make it 4-1 after being put through by Emerson in the dying seconds, but Verbruggen races out of his goal and saves his eventual effort.
FULL-TIME: BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION 1-3 WEST HAM
The Hammers win for the second Premier League game in a row after a brilliant 3-1 triumph at in-form Brighton.

The Irons took the lead at the Amex Stadium after 19 minutes, Antonio winning the ball high up the pitch before squaring for Ward-Prowse, who stroked home the rebound after seeing his initial effort blocked.

Brighton dominated possession but West Ham always looked a threat on the counter, and that was how they doubled their lead after the interval as Benrahma fed Bowen, who coolly poked past the debutant Verbruggen.
Things would get even better for the visitors moments later with Bowen again playing a big part, bringing the ball down before finding Antonio, who jinked past Webster before lashing home.
Brighton would pull a goal back through Gross' long-range effort, but it would prove just a consolation as Moyes' men saw it out to secure all three points.
West Ham remain unbeaten and move top of the Premier League, until Sunday at least, having picked up seven points from three matches.
They only picked up 40 points in the entirety of last season, and fans will be hoping they can continue their great start when they travel to take on newly promoted Luton Town next Friday.
For Brighton, it is a bump in the road after their own impressive start, and De Zerbi will be looking for a strong response when they host Newcastle United next weekend.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of West Ham's 3-1 Premier League victory over Brighton and Hove Albion at the Amex Stadium.
Goodbye!
